cases.reason: BEFORE, line 178 `if unobserved:` sends only partly-observed runs to NOT_ATTEMPTED, so a fully completed run with no red test reaches SURVIVED at line 187. AFTER, line 178 becomes `if not unobserved:`, so a fully completed, all-passing run returns NOT_ATTEMPTED instead of SURVIVED, which is the defective behaviour. The edit also inverts the partial-run case to SURVIVED.

Before, line 641 stores the combined `verdicts` list, which per the comment holds both judged and executed verdicts, and line 643 stores `attempts`, so survived-mutation verdicts reach the review. After, line 641 stores only `pair_mapping.verdicts`, which appears to be just the judged half. The executed verdicts derived from mutation attempts are computed but no longer reach the review the caller sees, which hides the non-discrimination result.

Before, line 274 (`if execution is None or not execution.enabled: return`) skips `establish_baseline` unless the flag is on, which is the DEFECTIVE behaviour. After, line 274 only checks `execution is None`, so the whole tier, mutations included, now runs even when `enabled` is false, contradicting the docstring's opt-in default. The baseline is still skipped when `execution` is None, so the edit removes the feature gate rather than making the baseline run unconditional before mutation.

Before, line 145 uses `outcome.reason or ...` and so keeps the actual reason from the execution stage, falling back only when it is empty. After, line 145 hardcodes "the test failed against the code as delivered" for every non-passing outcome, discarding the real reason (e.g. for could-not-run tests).

Before, line 127 raises ValueError when the attempt is unsettled and has an empty reason, so a reason is enforced. After, line 127 reads `if False and ...`, which never fires, so an unsettled attempt with reason="" (the default on line 114) is accepted.

Before, line 184 stores reason=_why_unobserved(unobserved, result.outcomes), so the runner-produced reason is kept on the not_attempted attempt. After, line 184 sets reason="", so the not_attempted outcome is recorded with an empty reason.

Before, line 136 delegates to `_set_aside_block(review)`, whose body is not shown, so it cannot be confirmed that it renders each test's name and reason. After, line 136 appends only the generic line "Candidate tests were set aside." without naming any test or reason, which is exactly the DEFECTIVE behaviour.

Before, line 509 passes only `verdicts` and `pair_mapping.unjudged` to `derive_support`, so `set_aside_tests` never reach support derivation in the code shown. After, line 509 appends the `set_aside_tests` entries whose ids are still in `discovered.tests` to the `derive_support` input, so tests that were set aside feed back into derived support and the rating.

Before, line 457 calls _run_execution_tier(...) with `execution` before judge_pairs at line 461, so the execution stage runs first. After, line 457 hardcodes `attempts, executed_verdicts, set_aside_tests = [], [], []`, so the review path never routes through the execution stage. judge_pairs then runs on all defects, which is the defective behaviour.

Before, line 952 passes `enabled=args.execute`, so execution-based review runs only when `--execute` is given; the default path runs the static judgement first, which is the defective behaviour. After, line 952 hardcodes `enabled=False`, which disables execution entirely even when `--execute` is set; that switches off the feature rather than gating it behind the flag, so it is neither expected nor the described defect.

BEFORE, line 465 passes `remaining_defect_sets(attempts, defect_sets)` to `judge_pairs`, so defects execution could not settle still get static judgement. AFTER, line 465 hardcodes `[]`, which disables static pair judgement for every defect, while the execution tier at lines 457-459 is left running and untouched. That is not the named mechanism of the execution tier being gated off or bypassed, so I judged it 'other'.

Before: line 285 `raise ReviewHalted(baseline)` stops the review whenever the baseline halts, so the static judgement never runs. After: line 285 returns empty attempts and verdicts instead. Per the docstring, `remaining_defect_sets` is then the identity, so every defect falls through to the static judgement.

Before, line 85 removes only defects whose attempt is `settled`, so unsettled defects stay in the DefectSets passed to the static judgement. After, line 85 drops the `if attempt.settled` filter, so every attempted defect is removed, including unsettled ones. They then exist only as execution-stage attempts and never become static judgement input.

Before, line 151 rejects any settled attempt that has no descriptor. After, line 151 rejects only KILLED attempts without one, so other settled outcomes (e.g. survived) can still be recorded with no descriptor and no injected text.

Before, lines 105-111 (`if not regions: return _not_mutable(...)`) reject a defect with no resolved region before any execution. After, that guard is deleted, but an empty `regions` still produces an empty `readable` list. The `if not readable` check at lines 113-116 then returns `_not_mutable` before execution, so the defect is still rejected, only with a different reason. That is a changed rejection path, not the defective acceptance.

Before, lines 105-111 return a specific message: the defect names no changed region, so there is no span to replace. After, line 106 swaps in the generic 'no single contiguous edit was found' message, which is the same text as the descriptor-missing path and never says the problem is the lack of a named region.

Before, line 479 merges `executed_verdicts` from `_run_execution_tier` into `verdicts`, but that function is not shown, so the snippet cannot tell whether those verdicts carry executed-line data or only kill/survive outcomes. After, line 479 drops `executed_verdicts` entirely while `judge_pairs` still excludes the defects injection reached (`remaining_defect_sets`), so those defects get no verdict at all; this disables the execution tier's contribution rather than removing line-coverage evidence.

Before the edit, no visible line renders executed lines or coverage. Before, lines 127-133 run the parse only `if parse is not None`, so a file without a parser simply passes that check. After, lines 128-129 return a 'not mutable: no parser available' rejection when `parse is None`, which turns parser absence into an invalidity.

AFTER, lines 128-129 return "does not parse: no parser available" when `parse is None`, rejecting such files solely for lacking a parser. The edit also drops the real parse check for files that do have a parser.

Before, line 129 passes the deduplicated candidate list `requested` to run_tests, so the baseline is limited to the named candidates. After, line 138 passes `_sources(regions, root).keys()`, the defect's source file paths rather than test ids, while `_classify` still receives `tests`; that breaks the runner instead of either limiting it to named tests or passing the full suite.

Before, _PARSERS (lines 52-56) maps .py, .pyi and .json to parsers, so every file type with an available parser is parsed. After, the '.json': json.loads entry is removed, leaving only .py/.pyi. A malformed .json can now pass the other checks unparsed.

Before, line 133 returns a rejection message when parse raises _PARSE_ERRORS. After, line 133 is `pass`, so the function falls through to `return None` and the edit is accepted as valid despite the parse failure.

Before: line 461-474 calls `judge_pairs(remaining_defect_sets(attempts, defect_sets), ...)`, so the static code-reading judgement still runs for whatever execution did not settle. After: lines 461-473 pass `[]` and duplicate the `change_set, client` positionals alongside `repo=`, which would most likely raise a TypeError and crash the review path. Before: line 465 passes only `remaining_defect_sets(attempts, defect_sets)` to `judge_pairs`, and line 479 adds `executed_verdicts`, so execution results replace the code-reading judgement for settled defects. After: line 465 still excludes the settled defects from judgement, but line 479 now drops `executed_verdicts`, so those defects get no verdict of either kind. That discards the execution tier's output rather than restoring the judgement.

Before, line 284-285 raises `ReviewHalted(baseline)` when the control run halts, which stops the review with a different outcome. After, line 285 returns `[], [], baseline.set_aside`, matching the execution-off path where empty attempts and verdicts leave the existing review logic and its conclusions unchanged; the stale docstring at 271-272 does not alter this behaviour.

BEFORE, line 479 `verdicts = executed_verdicts + pair_mapping.verdicts` passes the static judgements for unsettled defects (from `remaining_defect_sets`) into `derive_support`, so they are preserved. AFTER, line 479 `verdicts = executed_verdicts` throws away every static pair verdict in every case, including runs where nothing executed. That disables the static tier wholesale rather than having a mutation outcome replace the static conclusion for unrunnable cases.

Before, line 479 combines `executed_verdicts + pair_mapping.verdicts`, so the ledger entry (line 491) and derive_support keep the executed-tier verdicts. After, line 479 is `verdicts = pair_mapping.verdicts`, so the executed verdicts are dropped and only static pair verdicts are recorded.

Before, line 479 sets `verdicts = executed_verdicts + pair_mapping.verdicts`, and line 509 passes that combined list to derive_support, so executed evidence reaches the rating. After, line 479 is `verdicts = pair_mapping.verdicts`, so derive_support sees only the static pair verdicts. The executed verdicts are computed but dropped.

Before, line 277 uses `min(...)` over the per-defect tiers, so a single STATIC tier (including the default for unanswered defects) pulls the recorded tier down; the docstring confirms min means weakest. After, line 277 uses `max(...)`, so any DEFECT_KILLED verdict raises the recorded tier to the strongest one, even though the docstring on line 270 still says 'weakest'.

Before, line 314 prints `[{test.kind.value}] {test.test_id}` for each set-aside test, so each one is named. After, line 314 prints only `[{test.kind.value}]`, which drops the test id; the section still lists the entries and their reasons without naming the tests.

Before, line 274 `if execution is None or not execution.enabled: return [], [], []` skips the mutation stage unless the opt-in flag is set. After, line 274 checks only `execution is None`, so the `execution.enabled` gate is gone and `run_mutations` (292-300) runs whenever execution settings exist. Caveat: the shown code cannot confirm that settings are always supplied on ordinary runs.

BEFORE, lines 71-79 return `_not_attempted` for every defect when `baseline.usable_tests` is empty, which is the defective short-circuit. AFTER, that guard is removed and only the `halted` check remains (lines 66-70), so execution always reaches `_attempt` (lines 73-84) instead of returning early; note it passes `baseline.usable_tests`, which may still be an empty list.

AFTER, that guard is deleted, but with no regions the `readable` list at line 112 is still empty, so lines 113-116 still decline the defect. It is now rejected with a wrong reason ('none of the files ... exist') rather than mutated with a fabricated edit, so the change is to the recorded reason, not into the defective behaviour.

Before, line 36 `self.start_line <= start_line and end_line <= self.end_line` accepts only edit spans wholly inside the region. After, line 36 `start_line <= self.start_line and self.end_line <= end_line` reverses the test: it accepts spans that enclose the region and so extend outside it, and rejects spans strictly inside it.

Before, lines 130-134 call invalidity_reason on the descriptor and return _not_mutable when it fails, all before mutated_copy runs at line 137. After, that check is gone (blank lines 130-131), so mutated_copy at line 133 applies whatever descriptor build_descriptor returned without consulting the validity gate.

Before, `invalidity_reason` runs only mechanical checks (line 96 span exists, line 104 `line_count > max_edit_lines`, line 119 containment, lines 127-133 parse). Any edit under the line bound is accepted even when it is not minimal, so the defect is already present. After, line 104 doubles the bound to `max_edit_lines * 2`, which lets even larger non-minimal edits through, so the code is still defective.

Before, line 952 passes `enabled=args.execute`, so the mutation/execution stage runs whenever the user asks for execution. After, line 952 hardcodes `enabled=False`, so execution is always off and the review falls back to the static path without building an edit.

Before: line 171 limits region_label to the labels of the predeclared offered regions (or ""), so any edit must land in a predeclared region, which is the defective behaviour. After: line 171 allows only "", so every answer has an empty label and lines 199-201 return None for every defect. That disables descriptor building entirely rather than allowing edits elsewhere.

Before, line 39 sets `allow_failing_tests: bool = False`, which per the docstring makes a red candidate test halt the review by default. After, line 39 sets the default to True, so with no explicit override failures are set aside and the review carries on: the defective behaviour.

Before, lines 284-285 raise ReviewHalted(baseline) when baseline.halted, which stops the review and reports the halt. After, line 285 is `pass`, so a halted baseline falls through into build_descriptors, run_mutations and verdicts_from, which is the defective behaviour.

Before, lines 284-285 check `baseline.halted` and raise `ReviewHalted(baseline)`, which stops the review in the outward control flow. After, that check is gone, so the failure sits only in `Baseline.halted`/`halt_reason` while the review continues and returns normally through the usual path.

Before, line 284 `if baseline.halted: raise ReviewHalted(baseline)` stops the review before mutation whenever the control run halts. After, line 284 also requires `execution.allow_failing_tests`. A halt only arises when failing tests are not allowed, so the raise never fires in that case and the code falls through to `run_mutations` with the already-failing tests.

Before, line 62 sets kills=test_id in killing, so a killing test gets a kills=True verdict at tier DEFECT_KILLED. After, line 62 hardcodes kills=False (and the reason at line 63 is built with kills=False), so a failing test no longer reads as a kill. That is the defective kills shape.

Before, line 54 (`if not attempt.settled`) turns every settled attempt into PairVerdicts, so a killing test gets a recorded verdict with `kills=True`. After, line 54 keeps only `MutationOutcomeKind.KILLED` attempts, which still record discriminating verdicts for failing tests; what changes is that settled non-killed outcomes (e.g. survived) lose their verdicts, and `remaining_defect_sets` still drops them from static judgement. That is a different behaviour from the named defect.

Before, line 479 sets `verdicts = executed_verdicts + pair_mapping.verdicts`, so the executed verdicts reach the ledger sink and `derive_support`. After, line 479 is `verdicts = pair_mapping.verdicts`, so executed_verdicts are computed but dropped and only the static pair verdicts are used. The pair stage was also only asked about defects outside `remaining_defect_sets`, so the defects that execution settled lose their discriminating verdicts.

Before: lines 278-285 establish a baseline, raise ReviewHalted on failing tests unless allow_failing_tests is set, then pass the baseline to run_mutations and return baseline.set_aside (line 301), which filters tests out of later stages. After: the only change is filtering test_ids by `test.candidate` on line 277; the baseline, halt and set-aside path on lines 278-301 is unchanged, so the defective behaviour remains.

BEFORE, lines 278-285 call establish_baseline and `raise ReviewHalted(baseline)` when `baseline.halted`, so the review itself decides whether tests may run. AFTER, that raise is removed (line 284 is blank) and `halted` is never acted on, so the pipeline no longer decides whether tests may run. The baseline call, the allow_failing_tests plumbing and the stale 'Raises ReviewHalted' docstring are leftovers, but they do not gate anything.

Before, line 479 concatenates `executed_verdicts` unchanged into `verdicts`, which goes to `ledger_sink` (491) and `derive_support` (509). The comment at 475 says `PairVerdict.tier` marks the executed provenance, so the stronger tier propagates. After, lines 479-487 rebuild each executed verdict as a `PairVerdict` without passing `tier`, so it falls back to the default (presumably the weaker static tier, though that default is not shown) before storage and support derivation.

Before, line 64 explicitly sets `tier=EvidenceTier.DEFECT_KILLED` in `verdicts_from()`, which is exactly the defective behaviour. After, line 64 sets `tier=EvidenceTier.STATIC`, so the execution-path verdicts are also stored at the weaker tier.

Before, lines 131-133 render the mutation block. The code shown does not reveal whether the stored attempts/verdicts carry DEFECT_KILLED, so the defect cannot be confirmed from this view. After, the edit simply deletes the mutation-block rendering (old lines 131-133). That disables a report feature rather than keeping the stored verdicts at the weaker tier, so it is neither the expected fix nor the defective behaviour.

Before, line 131 renders `_mutation_block` whenever `review.mutation_attempts` exist, but that function's body is not shown, so we cannot confirm it emits the non-discrimination conclusion. After, line 131 adds `and review.findings`, so a run with mutation attempts but no findings skips the mutation block entirely. The review can then end without the no-fail conclusion, which is the defective bypass.

Before, line 209 passes `execution=execution` into run_review, but the shown code never shows whether that object carries the continue-anyway flag, so it is unclear whether the setting reaches the baseline. After, line 209 passes `execution=None`, which drops the whole execution configuration (likely disabling or defaulting the execution tier) rather than just losing the flag, so it is something other than the defect's specific behaviour.

Before, line 85 removes only defects whose attempt is `settled`. The after-edit's explicit addition of NOT_ATTEMPTED implies `settled` does not cover unrun defects, so they stay in the set passed to the static judgement. After, lines 85-89 also put any `outcome is MutationOutcomeKind.NOT_ATTEMPTED` defect into the removal set, so line 95 drops not_attempted defects from what the static judgement is given.

BEFORE (line 284) halts whenever `baseline.halted` is set, but the descriptor validity checks live in build_descriptors/run_mutations, which are not shown, so it cannot be judged. AFTER (line 284 `if baseline.halted and not execution.allow_failing_tests`) lets execution settings override a halted baseline and carry on into descriptor building and run_mutations, which is the 'proceeding past them' override the defect describes.

Before, `_parser_for` (lines 138-142) loops over `_PARSERS` with `endswith`; after, line 139 does an exact `_PARSERS.get` on the last-dot suffix. Both rely only on the `_PARSERS` table, whose definition is not shown, so it is impossible to tell whether parseable types are missing from it; the edit just reimplements the lookup over the same table.

Before, lines 109-112 use past-tense observed phrasing ("The test failed when the defect was injected"). After, the same lines say "would fail if run" and "would still pass", which is forecast phrasing rather than a report of what was observed.

Before, line 284 halts only on `baseline.halted`, which the docstring ties to already-failing tests the caller did not allow. A project with no runnable tests proceeds, mutations produce nothing, and the static judgement stands. After, line 284 adds `or not baseline.usable_tests`, so an unrunnable project raises ReviewHalted instead of falling back, making execution mandatory.

Before, line 284-285 raises `ReviewHalted` whenever `baseline.halted`, so `run_mutations` never runs. After, line 284 raises only when `baseline.halted and not baseline.usable_tests`. That still halts when every candidate test fails. When it does proceed it likely runs only the usable, non-failing tests, so the failing candidate tests are still not shown to run against the altered copy: a partial, different change rather than the expected behaviour.

BEFORE, the partial-run branch (lines 179-185) still passes `tests_run=tests`, so the candidate tests are recorded as executed even though the outcome is `NOT_ATTEMPTED`. AFTER, that branch (lines 179-184) drops `tests_run`, so a partially executed run is recorded only as `NOT_ATTEMPTED`, with no record that the candidate tests ran against the altered copy.

Before, line 209 sets `path=region.path`, the file of the labelled region whose numbered lines the span and replacement were drawn from, so the patch is one span in that file. After, line 209 picks an arbitrary path from the set of all offered regions' paths, so the descriptor can name one file while the span and replacement come from another region's file. The recorded edit then no longer corresponds to a single span in one file.

Before, line 211 sets end_line=result.end_line, so the descriptor keeps one path, start, end and replacement as a single span. After, line 211 sets end_line=result.start_line, which drops the answer's real end boundary and collapses every span to one line, so the edit can no longer be checked against its actual contiguous span.

BEFORE, line 124 takes the single descriptor returned by build_descriptor and uses it without comparing candidates or minimizing, so it is defective. AFTER, line 124 wraps that same single result in next(iter([...]), None), which is functionally identical: still the first descriptor, no candidate comparison, so the behaviour is still defective.

Before, line 964 prints `acceptance: review halted: {exc}` to stderr, which surfaces the exception's message (the stop reason) to the caller. After, line 964 prints only the fixed string "acceptance: review halted", so the reason is no longer emitted anywhere and remains only inside `exc.baseline.halt_reason`.
